AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEnteredLate.issue: Rollup of guards G1, G2 and G3 per binding rule 4. The loop's SHAPE is right -- up to 13 iterations, break on combat over / turn change / nothing playable, take the first playable card in hand, spend its energy, play it. Three things are wrong. (a) The hook is the LAST of three full passes in Hook.AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEntered (Hook.cs:928-955), entered strictly after turn_structure steps 22-24; the sim fires it from on_player_turn_started, sharing one registration-ordered pass with every step-22/23 listener (G1). (b) The plays go through CombatState.play_card, the MANUAL path, where C# uses CardCmd.AutoPlay with AutoPlayType.Default, so nothing downstream sees them as auto-plays (G2). (c) No card selector is installed where C# pushes VakuuCardSelector, so any selection screen a played card opens resolves RANDOMLY instead of deterministically (G3). Rule 7: Hook.cs, CombatManager.cs and audits/seam/turn_structure.json are NOT hashed by this record.

GetTarget.rationale: WhisperingEarring.cs:96-106: AnyEnemy -> `combatState.HittableEnemies.FirstOrDefault()` (the LEFTMOST living enemy, no RNG draw); AnyPlayer -> the owner; AnyAlly -> a Rng.CombatTargets pick among OTHER players; anything else -> null. The sim's play_card with target_idx omitted resolves 'the first living enemy' for ANY_ENEMY cards and None otherwise, which reproduces the first and last arms exactly and the third trivially (self-targeted cards hit the player). Load-bearing detail checked deliberately: because C#'s GetTarget already supplies a non-null target for AnyEnemy, CardCmd.AutoPlay's `Rng.CombatTargets.NextItem(HittableEnemies)` fallback (CardCmd.cs:73-77) is NOT reached, so neither side consumes a CombatTargets draw here -- which matters for RNG parity and is the opposite of the sim's own auto_play_card path (combat.py:540-546), which does draw. The AnyAlly arm is multiplayer-only: it filters to `c.IsPlayer && c != Owner.Creature` and the sim has exactly one player. Waived-by-scope inside a faithful entry rather than as its own waiver, since the reachable arms all match. Rule 7: combat.py and CardCmd.cs are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the relic's C# hook is the THIRD of three full listener passes, entered after the whole turn-start pass; the sim runs it inside that pass, so the outcome depends on the order of run.relics
guards.issue: MECHANISM: Hook.AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEntered runs AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEnteredEarly, then AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEntered, then AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEnteredLate as three separate complete passes (Hook.cs:928-955) -- PROMPT.md bug class 25 -- and CombatManager.RunAutoPrePlayPhase enters the phase strictly after Hook.AfterSideTurnStart and the orb queue (CombatManager.cs:556-572). The relic's own C# doc comment says why it chose Late: 'we want this to trigger after all other triggers fire'. The sim has neither the phase nor the pass structure (audits/seam/turn_structure.json step 26 and guard G8), so whispering_earring.py:27 fires from on_player_turn_started alongside every step-22 and step-23 listener in a single `for l in list(self._listeners)` loop (hooks.py:285-295). REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py tools/audit/relic_probes_b17.py earring-order): relics=['vexing_puzzlebox','whispering_earring'] has the Earring play the Puzzlebox's free card (['strike','strike','strike','defend','armaments']); reversed, the free card is added after the loop and never played (hand left as ['defend','armaments']). Same verdict, cited not re-derived. Second ported witness added here. Rule 7: Hook.cs, CombatManager.cs, hooks.py, audits/seam/turn_structure.json and audits/relic/crossbow.json are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE): the port routes an AUTO-play through the MANUAL play path, so nothing downstream can tell these plays were automatic
guards.issue: MECHANISM: WhisperingEarring.cs:79-80 does `await card.SpendResources()` and then `CardCmd.AutoPlay(choiceContext, card, target, AutoPlayType.Default, skipXCapture: true)`, which ends in `card.OnPlayWrapper(..., isAutoPlay: true, ...)` (CardCmd.cs:51-128) -- so the resulting CardPlay carries IsAutoPlay. whispering_earring.py:43 calls `combat.play_card(playable[0] - 1)`, the manual path (combat.py:381-421), even though the sim HAS an auto-play surface the Imbued enchantment already uses (CombatState.auto_play, combat.py:423-438, and auto_play_card, combat.py:516-546, which passes `auto_play=True` to should_play_card). REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py tools/audit/relic_probes_b17.py earring-auto): with relics=[whispering_earring, brilliant_scarf], Brilliant Scarf's counter reads 5 after the Earring's turn-1 loop, where C# leaves it at 0 because BrilliantScarf.AfterCardPlayed returns early on `cardPlay.IsAutoPlay` (BrilliantScarf.cs:84-87). Both relics are ported Ancients and co-obtainable. Every card the Earring plays therefore shifts which card Brilliant Scarf makes free, for the rest of that turn. RULE 3 boundary, stated explicitly: audits/relic/brilliant_scarf.json guard G1 verdicts 'the sim's on_card_played carries no auto-play flag' a LIVE gap, and this entry does NOT re-derive that; what this entry adds is a divergence in THIS relic's own port -- it manufactures manual plays where the game manufactures auto-plays, so even a fixed Brilliant Scarf would still count them. TWO SUB-CLAUSES CHECKED AND FOUND FAITHFUL, so they are not part of the gap: (i) the card SELECTION agrees, because C#'s `CanPlay()` asks Hook.ShouldPlay with AutoPlayType.None (CardModel.cs:1755) -- the manual arm -- so Enthralled (Enthralled.cs:21-38, ported at sts2_rl/cards/enthralled.py:41-46, the only ported ShouldPlay implementer that distinguishes the two) blocks the same cards on both sides, executed in the same probe; (ii) energy accounting agrees, because C#'s SpendResources -> SpendEnergy fires Hook.AfterEnergySpent with the real cost (CardModel.cs:1816-1843) and the sim's play_card fires on_energy_spent with the real cost (combat.py:411-412), so the ported listener sts2_rl/relics/intimidating_helmet.py:19-22 behaves identically. Rule 7: CardCmd.cs, CardModel.cs, combat.py, BrilliantScarf.cs, Enthralled.cs, sts2_rl/cards/enthralled.py, sts2_rl/relics/intimidating_helmet.py and audits/relic/brilliant_scarf.json are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: G3 (LIVE): C# pushes VakuuCardSelector for the whole loop, making every selection screen deterministic; the sim installs nothing and selects at random
guards.issue: MECHANISM: WhisperingEarring.cs:54 wraps the loop in `using (CardSelectCmd.PushSelector(new VakuuCardSelector()))`, and VakuuCardSelector.GetSelectedCards is `options.Take(maxSelect)` in row-major order (VakuuCardSelector.cs:17-20) -- fully deterministic, with no RNG draw. The port installs no selector, and CombatState.select_cards falls back to `self._rng.sample(candidates, count)` when `card_selector` is None (combat.py:560-581). REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py tools/audit/relic_probes_b17.py earring-auto): the Earring auto-playing Armaments (a ported Ironclad Common whose OnPlay opens an upgrade selection, sts2_rl/cards/armaments.py:41) upgrades twin_strike on seeds 0 and 3 and bash on seeds 1, 2 and 4, with `card_selector = None` in every case; C# always upgrades the FIRST option. Both sides ported and the pairing needs no second relic: Armaments reaches the opening hand from the starting deck or any card reward, and eight ported cards open selection screens from OnPlay (grep `select_cards|CardSelectCmd` over sts2_rl/cards/ -- armaments, brand, burning_pact, headbutt, colorless_attacks, colorless_skills x4). Two distinct observables, not one: the wrong card is picked, AND the sim consumes shared-RNG draws the game does not consume at all. Rule 7: VakuuCardSelector.cs, combat.py, sts2_rl/cards/armaments.py and the other card modules named are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: `CombatManager.Instance.IsPlayerReadyToEndTurn(player)` is one of the loop's three break conditions (WhisperingEarring.cs:64-67) and has no sim counterpart
guards.issue: The sim's loop breaks on `combat.is_over` and `self.turn != start_turn` (whispering_earring.py:38) but has no notion of a player having signalled 'end turn'. In the game this matters because the AutoPrePlay phase is asynchronous and the local player may already have pressed End Turn. DORMANT: the sim's driver is synchronous -- on_player_turn_started runs to completion inside PlayerCombatState.start_turn (player.py:185) before any agent action is possible, so no ready-to-end-turn state can exist while the loop runs, and there is no `ready_to_end_turn` concept anywhere in sts2_rl (grep returns nothing). Filed as a gap rather than a waiver because 'the sim has no such system' is a dormant gap under binding rule 1, not out of scope; what would make it live is any asynchronous or interruptible turn model. Rule 7: player.py is NOT hashed here.

guards.what: N2: the card the loop picks -- C#'s `pile.Cards.FirstOrDefault(c => c.CanPlay())` (WhisperingEarring.cs:72-73) vs the sim's first entry of valid_actions (whispering_earring.py:40-43)
guards.rationale: combat.valid_actions (combat.py:687-704) walks the hand in index order and admits a card when `card.is_playable`, `hooks.should_play_card(card)` and the hook-modified cost is affordable; `playable[0] - 1` is therefore the lowest playable hand index, matching FirstOrDefault over the hand pile. CanPlay's clause list (CardModel.cs:1734-1763) is the same set plus two the sim cannot reach: the Unplayable KEYWORD (the sim folds unplayability into `is_playable`) and `TargetType.AnyAlly && living player creatures <= 1`, which is multiplayer-only. Both break when nothing is playable. EXECUTED in the earring-auto probe via the Enthralled case, where both sides pick Enthralled itself first.

guards.what: N3: MAX_CARDS = 13 (whispering_earring.py:22) vs `public const int maxCardsToPlay = 13` and the literal `cardsPlayed < 13` (WhisperingEarring.cs:21, 58)
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file; 13 is unconditional and appears as a bare literal in the loop bound as well as in the named const. `for _ in range(self.MAX_CARDS)` gives the same 13 iterations, and each sim iteration corresponds to one C# `cardsPlayed++` even when the play is refused, because both count attempts rather than successes.
